To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we present a simple and accurate method to extract thermal resistance for SiGe HBTs from DC electrical measurements and that our approach is scalable and applicable to different device geometries.
the thermal resistance of a device is a function of temperature and the existing techniques in the literature do not take this dependence into account.
we have proposed a new extraction technique to estimate the thermal resistance that is scalable and accurate.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and validation of a novel extraction methodology to determine the self-heating of SiGe HBTs and the temperature dependent thermal resistance of SiGe HBFETs.

the development of a simple, accurate and reliable technique to extract the thermal resistance of SiGe HBTs from their measured DC electrical characteristics and the applicability of this method on measured data of fabricated SiGe HBT.

the development of an efficient extraction technique for the thermal resistance of SiGe HBTs from the DC electrical measurements and its validation with model card simulations and measurements of a SiGe BJT fabricated in STMicroelectronic B55 process.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
our extraction methodology provides a simple and accurate technique for extracting the self-heating effects of SiGe HBTs.

, for a given device geometry, the extraction methodology presented in this work can accurately extract the device thermal resistance from the DC electrical characteristics measured at different temperature levels.

, for a given technology, the thermal extraction methodology proposed in this paper is superior to the existing techniques and can be used to extract the thermal resistance with an accuracy of 10% or better.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
our approach is simple, scalable, accurate, and can be applied on measured data of any SiGe HBT.
our approach can be used for accurate extraction of the device self-heating thermal parameters from measured DC data of SiGe HBTs.
our approach is simple, scalable and accurate and can be used to extract the selfheating thermal resistance of SiGe HBTs from the measured DC data.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the existing techniques to extract self-heating thermal resistances from measured DC data suffer from a systematic deviation in the extracted values of the thermal resistances.
the temperature dependence of the thermal resistance is a function of the emitter area and the base doping.

the existing extraction techniques are highly sensitive to the temperature of measurement and therefore the accuracy of extracted thermal resistance is highly questionable when applied to the measured data of devices operating under high self-heating conditions.
